| An empty value | `--with: give a path, as --with=PATH or --with=PATH@BRANCH` |

"The repository under review" means the same folder in local and remote review,
and the same `owner/repo` from the remote in every mode. A companion whose
remote or default branch cannot be read is refused the same way, with
`--with: PATH:` before the reason.

## Companion pull requests

```sh
co-maintainer set --repo=owner/app --companions=owner/docs,owner/vscode-ext
```

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `companions` | none | Repositories, as `owner/repo`, whose pull requests a review of this one may read, up to 5 |

`--unset=companions` or a blank value clears it. `set` refuses a name that is
not `owner/repo`, the repository itself, a name given twice, and more than 5.

In the pull request body, one line per companion names its pull request:

```
Companion: owner/vscode-ext#45
Companion: owner/docs#112
```

- **A line counts anywhere in the body**, on a line of its own. The key is not
  case-sensitive.
- **Only listed repositories are read.** A line for a repository missing from
  `companions` is ignored. Without that rule, a pull request from a fork could
  name any repository the App can read, private ones included.
- **The branch name.** For a listed repository with no body line, the review
  looks for an open pull request with the same head branch name, among the
  first 500 open ones. One from a fork counts, and one from the companion
  repository itself wins. When there is
  none, the companion's COMPANION block says `no changes on this branch`, and it
  has no checkout to search.
- **Body lines win** over the branch name. At most 5 companions.
- **A closed or merged companion pull request** is still read, with its final
  diff.
- **Its files** come from the GitHub API, `pulls/N/files`, paginated.
- **Search** runs in a worktree of the companion pull request's head, made the
  same way as a pull request's own worktree: one blobless clone, reused. It is
  made on the first search of that companion.

In [PR review](local-pr-review.md) the companion pull requests are read with
your own GitHub auth, and `--with` adds local checkouts to them. A repository
given both ways is read once, from its checkout. `--with` companions come first
and count toward the limit of 5.

### In App review

An App client reads one installation, so each companion is read with the App
client of the installation that has the companion repository. The App must be
installed on the companion repository too, in the same account or another one.

When no installation can read a companion, or GitHub answers 403 or 404, the
review goes on without it. The job log on the dashboard gets the warning
`companion_unreachable`, which says "The companion owner/vscode-ext#45 could not
be read, so the review ran without it."

The GitHub review's Metadata block names the companions, body lines first:

```
- Companions: owner/vscode-ext#45, owner/docs (no matching pull request)
```

A companion that could not be read is shown as `owner/vscode-ext#45
(unreachable)`.

## What the model gets

Each companion gets a COMPANION block in the user prompt, after the
`WORKSPACE` or `PULL REQUEST` block and before the diff. It lists the changed
files with their status and line counts. Paths carry the repository name, so
they cannot collide with the reviewed change.

```
COMPANION owner/vscode-ext · branch feature/session-api · 3 files changed
owner/vscode-ext:src/client/session.ts   modified  +12 -4
owner/vscode-ext:src/client/api.ts       modified  +3 -1
owner/vscode-ext:package.json            modified  +1 -1

COMPANION owner/docs · branch main · no changes on this branch
```

- **About 100 characters per file.** A list stops at 200 files, or at
  24,000 characters of file lines, with `and N more`. A path longer than 200
  characters ends in `...`.
- **No change is information.** A companion with nothing on its branch says
  `no changes on this branch`.
- **One sentence comes first:** "COMPANION blocks list changes in other
  repositories that belong to this change. They are context. Report findings
  only on this repository's files, and name the companion file in the body when
  it is the reason."
- **The system prompt is the same bytes.** The cached prefix still hits, and a
  review without `--with` sends the same request as before.
- **The patches are not in the prompt.** The model reads them with
  `read-full-diff`, which takes a companion path such as
  `owner/vscode-ext:src/client/session.ts`, with `offset` and `limit`, under
  the same [cap on one answer](review.md#reading-the-rest-of-a-file).
- **Search.** `search-non-code` takes a `repo` argument. It is the repository
  under review when left out, or a companion's `owner/repo`. It searches the
  companion folder's tracked files as they are on disk, with that repository's
  own search settings, so the model can search a companion's docs even when the
  companion did not change. With `@BRANCH` the folder holds whatever branch is
  checked out, not `BRANCH`.

Companion content is untrusted, like pull request text. The model gets it as
data.

## Findings

A finding is anchored to the reviewed repository's files. For example, at the
line that removes `startSession()`: "This removes `startSession()`, but the
companion branch `owner/vscode-ext@feature/session-api` still calls it in
`src/client/session.ts`."

- **A finding the model places on a companion file** has no location. It is
  shown with the other findings, without a path or lines, labeled with the
  companion's name, for example
  ``[P2 · non-blocking] `owner/vscode-ext`: `src/client/session.ts:12` ``. In
  `--output=github` its annotation names no file or line. It is not carried to
  the next round.
- **Findings on the companion's own files** come from its own review, run in
  the companion with `--with` pointing back.

## Carry-over

Local review and PR review keep each companion in their carry record: the
repository, the branch, and a hash of its file list and patches. App review
keeps the same three in the stored round state, in `companions_json`.

When a companion changes, carried findings are checked again, even if the
reviewed repository did not change. Every file is sent again, and each carried
finding in an unchanged file gets the hint "file unchanged since the last
review, but a companion repository changed". Adding or leaving out a companion
counts as a change too. In App review a round where a companion changed
reviews the whole pull request, even when the repository's review scope is
incremental. Only a push or a review request starts an App round, so a change
in the companion pull request alone waits for the next one.

Remote review does not keep companions in its carry-over yet. A remote round
where only a companion changed reviews only what changed in the reviewed
repository. Use `--fresh` then.

## Output

- **`--json`** has `companions` when the review has any, and leaves it out
  otherwise:

  ```json
  "companions": [
    { "repo": "owner/vscode-ext", "branch": "feature/session-api", "source": "flag", "pr": null, "files": 3, "status": "read" },
    { "repo": "owner/docs", "branch": "feature/session-api", "source": "pr-body", "pr": 112, "files": 0, "status": "empty" }
  ]
  ```

  `source` is `flag`, `pr-body` or `branch-name`. `pr` is the companion pull
  request's number, or `null` for `--with` and when no pull request matched.
  `status` is `read`, `empty` when the branch has no change, or `unreachable`,
  with `branch` `null`. An unreachable companion also gives the warning
  `companion_unreachable`.
- **The terminal** prints one line under the header:
  `Companions: owner/vscode-ext@feature/session-api (3 files) · owner/docs@main (no changes)`.
- **`--output=github`** prints the same line in the job summary.

## Privacy

The visibility of the reviewed repository and of each companion is read from
the GitHub API at review time, with your own GitHub auth. App review reads a
companion's visibility with the App client that read the companion. A companion
whose visibility cannot be read counts as private.

A private companion in the review of a public repository is context and is
never quoted. Its patches and its search results go through the
[copied-passage check](review.md#mcp-servers): any run of 8 or more words a
finding copies from them is replaced with `[private context removed]`, and the
review adds a `private_text_removed` warning that says the passage came from a
private companion. A companion in the review of a private repository is not
checked.

File paths and names, such as `src/client/session.ts`, can appear in a finding.
The COMPANION block lists them, and the check does not cover them.

## Remote review

The client builds the companion diffs from `--with` on your machine and sends
them with the review. The client reads the visibility, and tells the server
which companions are private.

- **The handshake** lists `companions` among its features. A client that does
  not find it sends no companion and adds the warning `companions_unsupported`,
  which says "This server (version X) does not read companions, so the review
  ran without them." The review runs. An older client with a newer server sends
  none, and nothing changes.
- **The limit.** The server takes at most 500,000 characters of companion
  patches in total. Above that it keeps every file list, drops every patch, and
  adds the warning `companion_list_cut`. It also takes at most 1,000 files of
  one companion. The client sends the first 1,000 of a longer list, with the
  same warning.
- **Search** runs on your machine, in the companion checkout, through the same
  `search-non-code` tool call with its `repo` argument.

## Cost

About 100 characters per companion file, sent again in every round. Reads of
companion files are capped like any `read-full-diff` answer, and search results
go through the [tool limits](review.md#tool-limits).

A companion pull request costs a few GitHub API calls in every round: the pull
request or the branch name lookup, its files, and its visibility.

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/serve.md

# `serve`

Long-running process for **self-hosted** co-maintainer: GitHub App webhooks,
background review jobs, the [dashboard](dashboard.md), and the API used by
[remote review](remote-review.md). One binary, one `app.db`, one config dir.

Linux (WSL included) is the recommended platform. See
[dashboard: Linux](dashboard.md#linux) for why.

## What it does

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  gh[GitHub App]
  gh -->|POST webhook| serve[co-maintainer serve]
  serve --> jobs[Review and reply jobs]
  serve --> dash[Dashboard UI]
  serve --> remote[Remote review API]
  jobs -->|App token| gh
  browser[Browser] --> dash
  cli[CLI review --remote] --> remote
```

| Piece | Role |
| ----- | ---- |
| `POST /github/webhook` | PR and conversation events enqueue work |
| Dashboard at `/` | Per-repo init/sync, settings, activity, credentials |
| Job worker | Auto PR reviews, setup jobs, conversation replies |
| Remote review | Shared repo context for laptops without local init |

Team flow: configure the App once, run `serve`, add repos on the dashboard,
then either webhooks review PRs or developers use [`review --remote`](remote-review.md).
CLI-only users can ignore `serve` until they need shared context or automation.

## Before you run

| Check | Why |
| ----- | --- |
| [Install](getting-started.md#install) `co-maintainer` | `serve` is a CLI command |
| GitHub App (optional at startup) | Add it later in the dashboard **Settings**, or with `co-maintainer set` ([Configuration](configuration.md)). Changes apply without a restart. The dashboard can also create it for you (see [Create the App from the dashboard](#create-the-app-from-the-dashboard)) |
| `--github-webhook-secret=` (recommended) | Verifies webhook payloads |
| AI and GitHub access via dashboard **Get started** (`/setup`) or **Settings** | Reviews need models and repo access (can finish after first boot) |
| Public URL for webhooks (production) | GitHub must reach `POST .../github/webhook` |
| Linux or WSL for production | Other platforms log a warning and continue |

## Usage

```sh
co-maintainer set --github-app-id=... --github-app-private-key-file=./app.pem
co-maintainer set --github-app-id=... --github-app-private-key-path=./app.pem
co-maintainer set --github-webhook-secret=...
co-maintainer serve --port=5000

co-maintainer serve --port=5000 --password=your-dashboard-secret
co-maintainer serve --port=5000 --webhook-url=https://example.com/github/webhook
```

`--github-app-private-key-file` copies the key into `config.json`.
`--github-app-private-key-path` stores only the path, so the key stays on disk
and is read at startup. If that file is missing, `serve` warns and continues.
See [Configuration: App private key](configuration.md#app-private-key-inline-file-contents-or-path).

On non-Linux platforms, `serve` logs a one-line warning that Linux (WSL
included) is recommended, with a link to
[docs](https://co-maintainer.com/docs/troubleshooting.html). Nothing is blocked.

At startup, `serve` prints `app.db` path, dashboard URL, and webhook URL. On the
first start with password auth on it also generates a dashboard password and
prints it once. The password is stored in `config.json` as a hash, so later
starts keep it.

## Parameters

| Flag | Meaning |
| ------ | ----- |
| `--port=N` | HTTP port (required, 1 to 65535) |
| `--password=...` | Replace the stored dashboard password on every start, which signs every session out. A random one is generated on the first start if none exists. Leave it out of a service file and change the password in Settings |
| `--webhook-url=...` | Public webhook URL GitHub should use (also `CM_WEBHOOK_URL` or saved in Settings) |
| `--disable-auth=password` | Turn off password sign-in for this run |
| `--enable-auth=github` | Turn on GitHub OAuth sign-in for this run |
| `--trust-proxy` | Trust `x-forwarded-for` and `x-forwarded-proto` from a reverse proxy in front (also `CM_TRUST_PROXY=1`, see [Behind a reverse proxy](#behind-a-reverse-proxy)) |
| `--inject-500` | Every mutating `/api/*` call returns 500 (failure UI testing, also `CM_INJECT_500=1`) |
| `CM_REMOTE_BYOK_POLICY` | Whether a remote review may bring its own AI key: `off` (the default), `allow` or `require`, see [your own key](remote-review.md#your-own-ai-key) |
| `CM_REMOTE_CLIENT_TOOLS_POLICY` | Whether a remote review offers the model the tools a client declares, such as its own MCP servers: `off` (the default) or `on`, see [client tools](remote-review.md#your-own-mcp-servers-as-client-tools) |
| `CM_EXTENSIONS_DISABLED` | `1` turns [extensions](extensions.md) off: `register` refuses and no review runs one. The Cloud image sets it from outside the container |
| `CM_MCP_DISABLED` | `1` turns [MCP servers](review.md#mcp-servers) off: `set --mcp-config` refuses and no review starts one. The Cloud image sets it from outside the container |
| `CM_UPDATE_URL` | The host's update address. Turns on the daily check for a newer stable release and the dashboard's **Update** button, which POSTs the target version there. Unset, nothing calls out, see [Dashboard: Updates](dashboard.md#updates) |
| `CM_LOGIN_HINT` | Text shown on the sign-in page instead of the default "printed when `serve` started" line. Useful when a deployment hands out its own password, as the Cloud image does. Escaped as plain text |

Per-run `--disable-auth` / `--enable-auth` override values from `co-maintainer
set`. At least one sign-in method must stay enabled.

Persistent App, webhook, OAuth, and webhook URL fields: [Configuration](configuration.md)
and dashboard **Settings**.

## Sign in to the dashboard

**Password (default).** Copy the password from the `serve` console on first start,
or set it with `--password=...` or `co-maintainer set --password=...`. Change it
any time from **Settings**, which also signs out the other browser sessions.

**GitHub sign-in (optional).** One allowed GitHub user can sign in with the App's
OAuth client (no separate OAuth App).

**A one-time link (from the server).** Anyone with a shell on the server, a
script or an agent among them, can sign in without the password:

```bash
co-maintainer login-link
```

It prints one address, such as `https://review.example.com/login/link#...`.
Open it, then press **Sign in**. The link works once, for 5 minutes, and only on
that address. A new link replaces the old one, and a password change ends it.
Opening the link only shows the button, so a chat or mail preview cannot use it
up. The part after `#` never reaches the server or a proxy log. Making and
using a link are in the audit log, the link itself never is. It works with
password sign-in turned off too. The address comes from `CM_WEBHOOK_URL` or the
saved webhook URL. `serve --webhook-url` is not visible to another command, so
pass `--origin=https://your-address` then, or `--origin=http://localhost:PORT`
on a local server. `serve` must be running, with the same version.

1. On the GitHub App settings page, set **Redirect URL** to
   `http://<host>:<port>/auth/github/callback` (same host and port as `serve`).
2. Copy client ID and client secret from that page.
3. Save credentials and the allowed username:
   ```sh
   co-maintainer set --github-oauth-client-id=... \
     --github-oauth-client-secret=... \
     --github-oauth-allowed-user=your-github-username
   ```
4. Enable on the command line when needed:
   ```sh
   co-maintainer serve --port=5000 --enable-auth=github
   co-maintainer serve --port=5000 --disable-auth=password --enable-auth=github
   ```

OAuth and auth toggles can also be changed later in dashboard **Settings**. UI
routes and failure behavior: [Dashboard](dashboard.md).

The sign-in page says "Use the dashboard password printed when serve started."
Set `CM_LOGIN_HINT` to replace that line with your own text, for example a
pointer to the password your deployment already gave the user. It is shown as
plain text and escaped, so it cannot inject markup.

## Create the App from the dashboard

Creating an App by hand means copying a private key, a webhook secret, and OAuth
credentials between GitHub and the dashboard, and the webhook secret is easy to
mismatch. The GitHub App card in **Settings** can create the App for you instead:

1. Set a public **Webhook address** first. On `http://localhost:<port>...` the
   button explains that GitHub cannot reach it, so nothing silent happens.
2. Pick an **App name**. It defaults to `co-maintainer-<host>` and must be unique
   on GitHub, which the field lets you change.
3. Click **Create GitHub App**. The dashboard opens GitHub's manifest page, which
   asks you to confirm the permissions and events listed there.

GitHub then redirects back, and `serve` writes the App ID, private key, webhook
secret, and OAuth client ID and secret straight into `config.json`, the same keys
the manual fields use. The browser lands on the App's install page, where you
choose the repositories the App can see. The manual fields stay available for an
App you created yourself.

The manifest requests only what the code calls:

| Permission | Why |
| ---------- | --- |
| `contents: read` | Read the review guide, file contents, and git trees |
| `pull_requests: write` | Read a pull request, post reviews and review comments |
| `issues: write` | Post and read issue comments |
| `checks: write` | Create and update the review check run |
| `metadata: read` | Required by every App |

Events: `pull_request`, `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`,
`issue_comment`. GitHub delivers `installation` and `installation_repositories`
without a subscription, so the manifest does not list them.

## Webhook URL

Point the GitHub App webhook at:

`http://<host>:<port>/github/webhook`

The dashboard **Settings** field, `--webhook-url=...`, `CM_WEBHOOK_URL`, or
saved config override the default `http://localhost:<port>/github/webhook`.

When a secret is configured, `serve` checks `x-hub-signature-256`. Duplicate
delivery IDs are ignored. `pull_request` and review-comment events enqueue jobs
when the repo is active and rules allow it. Enable **Issue comments** and
**Issues: write** on the App if you want `@co-maintainer` conversation replies.
A reply on a finding's thread knows the rules the finding rests on, with
their text and links, so it can say which rule a finding follows.
When a reply on a finding's thread agrees that the finding was wrong, the
finding closes at once. A later round does not raise it again while its lines
are unchanged.

Manual PR review from the UI when GitHub cannot reach your host:
[Dashboard: Pull requests](dashboard.md#routes).

## Behind a reverse proxy

Put `serve` behind nginx, Traefik, Caddy, or a load balancer and start it with
`--trust-proxy` (or `CM_TRUST_PROXY=1`). Two things change:

- **Client address.** Sign-in lockout counts failed attempts per address. Without
  the flag every visitor arrives from the proxy's address, so five wrong guesses
  from anyone lock the owner out. With it, `serve` uses the last address in
  `x-forwarded-for`, the one your proxy appended, and ignores anything a visitor
  put to its left. A value that is not an IP address is ignored.
- **Secure cookies.** When the last `x-forwarded-proto` is `https`, the session
  cookie is sent with the `Secure` flag.

Only turn this on when a proxy you control sits in front and sets both headers.
Without one, a visitor could send the headers themselves.

## Run with Docker

Each release is also published as an image at
`ghcr.io/groophylifefor/co-maintainer`, tagged with the version and, for stable
releases, `latest`. It bundles Node.js, `git`, and the codegraph binary that
reviews use.

```sh
docker run -d --name co-maintainer -p 5000:5000 \
  -v co-maintainer-data:/data \
  -e CM_WEBHOOK_URL=https://example.com/github/webhook \
  ghcr.io/groophylifefor/co-maintainer:latest

docker logs co-maintainer
```

The first start prints the dashboard password in the logs. To choose it yourself,
set it on the volume before the first start:

```sh
docker run --rm -v co-maintainer-data:/data \
  ghcr.io/groophylifefor/co-maintainer:latest set --password=your-dashboard-secret
```

- Everything lives in the `/data` volume: `config.json`, `app.db`, generated
  guides, and repository clones. Keep it to survive upgrades.
- The container listens on port `5000` and runs as the non-root `node` user
  (uid 1000). A bind mounted host folder must be writable by that user.
- The image runs `serve --port=5000` by default. Any other command works too,
  for example `... set --token=...`. The health check assumes port `5000`.
- Run one container per volume. Only one `serve` may write to an `app.db`.
- Upgrade by pulling the new tag and recreating the container with the same
  volume. Queued jobs that were interrupted are picked up again on start.

- **Inline, file, and path.** `set` writes the App private key three ways:
  inline, as file contents, or as a path. The path form keeps the key out of
  `config.json`, and a missing file is warned about at startup. See
  [Configuration: App private key](configuration.md#app-private-key-inline-file-contents-or-path).

## Extensions

`serve` runs the [extensions](extensions.md) registered in its own `config.json`
in the reviews it posts as the GitHub App and in remote reviews. Register them on
the `serve` host with `co-maintainer extension register`. The command runs as the
user that runs `serve` and can read that user's files, `config.json` included.
`CM_EXTENSIONS_DISABLED=1` turns them off. On start, `serve` removes the run
folders of extensions that are no longer running, and nothing else.

## MCP servers

`serve` starts a repository's [MCP servers](review.md#mcp-servers) in the
reviews it posts as the GitHub App and in remote reviews, from its own
`config.json`. Set them on the `serve` host with
`co-maintainer set --repo=owner/repo --mcp-config=./mcp.json`. The servers run
as the user that runs `serve`, with only their own `env`, `PATH` and `HOME`.

A pull request from a fork gets no MCP tools, because anyone can open one and
its diff could try to steer the model toward the private context. Turn them on
for one repository with:

```sh
co-maintainer set --repo=owner/repo --mcp-allow-forks=true
```

`CM_MCP_DISABLED=1` turns MCP off on the host.

## Updating

Forward-only migrations: do not install an older CLI after a newer one has
opened `app.db`.

1. Stop `serve`.
2. `npm install -g co-maintainer@latest`
3. Start `serve` again with the same data directory.

Restart after upgrading. Do not reinstall while the old process is still
running. Same steps are listed on [Dashboard: Updating](dashboard.md#updating).

A review that was running when `serve` stopped is picked up on the next start,
before the server listens. One still reading the pull request is reviewed again.
One GitHub already took is kept, with no second review. One GitHub never got is
marked failed, its check run says the commit was not reviewed, and **Retry** on
the dashboard runs it again.

GitHub does not send a webhook again when the server missed it. So on start,
`serve` also looks at the pull requests it reviewed in the last 14 days, at
most 50. When its review still asks for changes and the author pushed while it
was down, the new commit is queued for review under the same rules as a push.
When a blocking finding was closed but the approval never reached GitHub, the
approval is posted once. A pull request closed while it was down is left alone.

A Docker server pulls the new image and starts the container again on the same
volume, with the options it started with. **Settings**, **Server**, **Updates**
shows those lines. When the host sets `CM_UPDATE_URL`, the dashboard also says
when a newer release is out and offers an **Update** button, see
[Dashboard: Updates](dashboard.md#updates).

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/dashboard.md

# Dashboard

Web UI started by [`serve`](serve.md). Use it to finish setup, add repositories,
run [`init`](init.md) / [`sync`](sync.md), tune auto-review, watch jobs, and
manage [remote review](remote-review.md) tokens. Webhooks and the job worker run
in the same process as the UI.

## What it is for

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  login[Sign in] --> setup["Get started (/setup)"]
  setup --> add[/repos/new/]
  add --> init[Init job on Activity]
  init --> ready[Repo overview]
  ready --> auto[Repo settings: auto-review]
  ready --> pr[Pull requests: manual review]
  ready --> tok[Settings: remote tokens]
  tok --> remote[Developers: review --remote]
```

| Goal | Where to go |
| ---- | ----------- |
| First-time server setup | **Get started** on home or `/setup`, then **Settings** |
| Onboard a repo | **Add repository**, wait on **Activity** |
| Refresh guides after `main` moves | Repo **Overview** or **Settings** (Sync), or a cron schedule in repo **Settings** ([Scheduled sync](sync.md#scheduled-sync)) |
| Team laptops without local init | **Settings** remote tokens, repo **Remote** tab |
| Debug a failed job | The open failures count beside **Activity**, then the job page |
| Find every finding of a kind | **Findings** in the left menu, or a repository's **Findings** tab |
| See who changed what | **Settings**, **Audit log** |

## Before you open

| Check | Why |
| ----- | --- |
| [`serve`](serve.md) is running | Dashboard is not a separate install |
| Dashboard URL from startup log | Default `http://localhost:<port>/` |
| Password or GitHub sign-in | See [Sign in](#sign-in) and [`serve`: Sign in](serve.md#sign-in-to-the-dashboard) |
| Browser on a host that can reach the server | Same network or VPN as production |
| A webhook URL GitHub can reach | The repo **Overview** warns when it cannot |

`/dashboard` redirects to `/`.

## Webhook reachability

A fresh `serve` defaults to `http://localhost:<port>/github/webhook`, which
GitHub cannot route to, so automatic reviews silently never arrive. Every repo
**Overview** states this: a bad-address notice when the configured webhook URL
host is loopback, `0.0.0.0`, or a private range, and a "No webhook delivery
yet" notice when nothing has been received. Both name the current URL and link
to **Settings**.

Once a delivery has arrived, the page shows **Last webhook delivery** instead.
The check only inspects the host. A single-label internal name and any public
host pass, and `serve` and `set` still accept every URL they did before.

## Adding a repository

**Add repository** runs the same read-only probe the CLI runs, server side,
then shows the recommended `init` command with its time, GitHub calls and
cost, a faster option when the run would take more than 30 minutes, and what
one pull request review costs. The numbers are the ones the CLI prints.
Nothing is written until **Add and start init** is
pressed, and that confirmation stores the plan's flags, limits and sources for
the repo before the init job is queued, so the run matches what was approved.

The estimate says whether it used this repository's recorded jobs or the
cm-dx-lab calibration, and whether it priced dollars from OpenRouter. See
[`probe`](probe.md) for how the recommendation is derived.

The same step asks who gets a review. It lists the [review policy](review-policy.md)
templates with a sentence each. The server default is selected and you decide.
Leaving it on the server default keeps the repository following it.

## Sign in

Open `http://<host>:<port>/`.

- **Password**: printed once on the first `serve` start, or set with `--password=...`. Change it in **Settings**.
- **GitHub** (optional): **Continue with GitHub** for the one allowed user.
  OAuth setup lives on [`serve`](serve.md#sign-in-to-the-dashboard).

Sessions use an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie (`Secure` on HTTPS).

## Get started (`/setup`)

`/setup` is a step by step wizard. The progress across the top names every
step and marks the done ones, and each step is its own URL (`/setup?step=ai`),
so **Back** and **Next** are plain links.

| Step | Done when |
| ---- | --------- |
| Models and API key | A provider and key are saved |
| GitHub access | `gh` or a personal access token is set |
| GitHub App and webhook | The App is saved and GitHub has delivered a webhook (see [Webhook reachability](#webhook-reachability)) |
| First repository | A repository has its guides |
| How reviews look (optional) | The blocking rule is saved |

Without a step in the URL the wizard opens on the first step that is not done.
A done step says **Done** and **Next**, a step that is not done offers its fix
and **Skip for now**. The last step shows a review comment with two sample
findings next to the options, and the preview follows them as you change them:

- **Blocking rule**: the model decides, or by severity (P0 and P1 block). It is
  the server default, saved with **Save blocking rule**. A repository's own rule
  still wins.
- **Diagram language**: Mermaid, PlantUML or a PlantUML server image.
- **References in the comment**: shown or left out.

Diagram language and references are set per repository, in its **Repository
settings** under **Review tools and limits** or with `set --repo`, so the
wizard only previews them.

The home page shows a **Setup is not finished** banner with the count of the
four required steps until they are done, and the menu shows the same count
(`2/4`). The optional step is not counted.

## Routes

The left menu holds **Repositories**, **Activity**, **Findings**, **Usage**,
**Setup** and the **Settings** pages, with **Audit log** among them.

| Path | Purpose |
| ---- | ------- |
| `/` | Repository list with reviews, open failures and cost of the last 30 days, the setup banner until setup is done, **Add repository** |
| `/setup` | The setup wizard |
| `/repos/new` | Pick an App-installed repo, **Preview** the plan, then confirm to start **init** |
| `/repos/:owner/:repo` | Overview: 30-day stats, findings by severity, recent pull requests, drift **Update now**, a short commit watch status line, webhook reachability and last delivery |
| `/repos/:owner/:repo/pulls` | Open pull requests with a **Review** button each, paged review history, manual **Review** by number when webhooks fail. A click on a row opens that pull request |
| `/repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/:n` | One pull request: title, rounds, findings with their state, references, job logs and each round's [extension](extensions.md) results |
| `/repos/:owner/:repo/findings` | The [Findings list](#findings) of this repository |
| `/repos/:owner/:repo/remote` | Remote CLI reviews for this repo (last 30 days) |
| `/repos/:owner/:repo/knowledge` | Generated guides (including **Repository instructions** when the repository has an `INSTRUCTIONS.md`), **Sync**, **Clear** |
| `/repos/:owner/:repo/settings` | **Who gets a review** (the [review policy](review-policy.md)), review scope, codegraph, analysis limits, schedule, remove repo |
| `/repos/:owner/:repo/pushes` | [Commit watch](commit-watch-review.md) setup and push reviews: range, App or CI, status, findings by severity, issues opened, cost |
| `/findings` | The [Findings list](#findings) across every repository |
| `/activity` | Every job, one row per review, with [filters](#activity), the failed list and **Pull requests we skipped** |
| `/activity/:id` | One job: its log, a [warning banner](#job-page) when it finished with a problem, links to the pull request page and the posted review |
| `/usage` | [Usage](#usage) for 7, 30 or 90 days, by repository and author, with **Export CSV**. `/analytics` redirects here |
| `/settings/...` | One page per settings section, see [Settings](#settings-global) |
| `/settings/audit` | The [Audit log](#audit-log) |

Every repository tab starts with the same breadcrumb, then the title, then the
tabs: **Overview**, **Pull requests**, **Findings**, **Knowledge**, **Remote
reviews**, **Pushes**, **Repository settings**. The commit watch setup lives on
**Pushes**, and the overview keeps one status line that links there.

A review stores the pull request title and author, so lists show
`#136 Rename format to formatDuration` without asking GitHub. A pull request
reviewed before 0.7.15 shows its number until its next review or first visit.

## Every count opens its list

No count of findings, failures or reviews is plain text. The **Result** column
on **Activity** opens the pull request page at that round. The overview
**Findings** card opens the repository's findings list, and each severity opens
it filtered to that severity. The recent pull requests' severity badges, the job
page **Found** card, and the Usage cards and severity rows do the same.

## Findings

**Findings** in the left menu lists every finding of every review, one row per
finding, with a repository filter. A source filter narrows it to pull request
reviews, pushes, remote reviews, CLI reviews, or the findings
[extensions](extensions.md) added. A finding with no pull request opens the
review that found it. **Close** closes a finding as accepted risk or will not
fix and asks why, **Reopen** opens a closed or withdrawn one again, see
[Closing a finding](review-policy.md#closing-a-finding). Each repository has the same list
on its **Findings** tab. A finding carried from round to round is one row, with
the state it has now.

| Column | What it shows |
| ------ | ------------- |
| Severity | P0 to P3 |
| Blocking | Whether it blocks under the repository's blocking rule |
| State | Open or Closed |
| Finding | The title, the file and line, and the pull request with its title and round |
| When | When that round ran |

Filters live in the URL, so a filtered list is a link: severity, state (open by
default), pull request, file text, author, and a search over the title and body.
Each value shows as a chip you can take off. A row opens the pull request page
at that finding.

## Pull request page

The title shows the pull request title. Each round has an anchor (`#round-4`)
and each finding one too, which the counts elsewhere link to. The findings header
says how many are open and closed, and every finding carries its state badge.
`file:line` opens the line on GitHub at the round's commit, and a finding that was
posted links its GitHub review thread. **References (N)** counts the references it
lists. Each row of the **Reviews** table opens that round's job log.

## Activity

Activity shows one row per review: the pull request, the result, the cost, the
time and the status. Every row opens its log. Other jobs, such as init, sync,
skip and reply, keep one row each. A review, init or sync run from the CLI is a
row too, once it is over, with its cost. The CLI writes it next to a running
`serve`, so it shows up without a restart. Job kinds, skip reasons and cancel reasons
read as sentences, for example "Skipped: nothing new since the last review".

Filters live in the URL as chips: status (running, done, failed, canceled,
skipped), kind, repository, pull request, a day range and a search box. The list
is paged.

The open page polls a small change stamp every 5 seconds and fetches the list
only when something changed. It waits while rows are selected or a field of the
list is in use, so a refresh never drops your work.

**Pull requests we skipped** has column headings, says why a row has no
repository, merges repeats within the same minute into one row with a count, and
hides the bot's own comments behind **Show own comments**.

### Failures

The red count beside **Activity** in the menu, for example `5 open failures`,
counts failures of the last 30 days that nobody dismissed and no later review
resolved. The home list and the repository overview show the same count for each
repository. Each of them opens the failed list for the same window, so the count
is the number of rows it opens.

Each failed row shows its reason with **Retry** and **Dismiss**. **Dismiss**
marks the failure as seen and keeps it in the history. **Dismiss all** does it
for every failure the list shows. A later successful review of the same pull
request resolves its earlier failures by itself. The failed list leaves out
dismissed and resolved failures and links to them in one click.

### Bulk select

Rows have checkboxes, and the header box selects every row on the page. The bar
above the list offers **Retry** and **Dismiss** for the selection, each enabled
only when a selected row allows it.

### Keyboard shortcuts

Activity, Findings and the Pull requests tab share these keys. A small bar at the
bottom of the list names them, and they never fire while you type in a field.

| Key | Action |
| --- | ------ |
| `j` / `k` | Move down and up |
| `Enter` | Open the row |
| `x` | Select the row (Activity) |
| `/` | Focus the search box |
| `?` | Show the shortcuts panel |

## Job page

A job that finished but logged a warning or an error gets a banner at the top
that says what went wrong and how to fix it, for example a check run update that
failed with 404 because the GitHub App lacks **Checks: Read and write**. Its
Activity row gets a warning mark too. A review job links the pull request page
and the GitHub review it posted. The log's **Clear** button shows only while the
job runs.

## Usage

Usage covers 7, 30 or 90 days. A repository filter and an author filter sit next
to the range, and the range links keep them. The author is the GitHub login that
opened the pull request, so CLI reviews and init or sync runs, which have none,
drop out when an author is chosen.

Every figure is the whole bill: **Spent**, each repository, each day and each
model include knowledge builds, replies and watch comments next to the
reviews. **By kind** lists them on their own rows, and keeps stopped reviews,
push reviews, remote reviews and CLI reviews apart from the posted pull request
reviews. A repository removed from the dashboard stays on Usage, marked
removed. **Worth a look** shows the same open failures the menu badge counts,
and dismissing one there dismisses it everywhere.

**Export CSV** downloads what the page counts, one row per review and one per
knowledge build, reply or watch comment:

```text
time,repository,pull_request,author,model,tokens_in,tokens_out,cost_usd,billed_to,findings,status,kind,branch,extensions_cost_usd
```

`kind` is `pr`, `push`, `remote`, `local`, `cli_pr`, `knowledge`, `reply` or
`watch`. `extensions_cost_usd` is the part of `cost_usd` the review's
extensions spent.

An unknown cost is an empty cell, never a zero. The failed attempts on the
**Reviews** card open every failed review of the range, dismissed ones too.

## Settings (global)

Each section is its own page in the left menu:

| Page | What you configure |
| ---- | ------------------ |
| AI models | Provider (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenCode Zen or OpenCode Go, see [AI providers](providers.md)), token, high model (reviews and synthesis), low model (history extraction). No model is pre-filled |
| GitHub | `gh` or PAT for init/sync and server-side Git reads, the GitHub App (**Create GitHub App**) and the webhook URL |
| Review defaults | Limits for new repositories, the [review policy](review-policy.md) template they start with, and the blocking rule every repository uses unless it has its own |
| Remote access | `cmr_…` tokens (secret shown once, with copy) and the **Client key policy (BYOK)**, see [your own key](remote-review.md#your-own-ai-key) |
| Server | Version, port and data folder, [Updates](#updates), the job queue and remote limits |
| Sign-in | Password vs GitHub sign-in toggles, and the password. A change applies to the next request, without a restart, and signs out the sessions opened before it. A `serve` flag (`--disable-auth`, `--enable-auth`) still wins |
| Extensions | Register, enable, disable and remove [extensions](extensions.md) |
| Audit log | Who did what, see [Audit log](#audit-log) |
| Danger zone | **Clear all knowledge** |

Saving PAT, App key, or OAuth values is validated against GitHub first. Bad
scopes return **422** and nothing is stored. A key or model is checked with
the provider the same way `set` checks it, and a rejected one is not stored.

Emptying a model, App ID or OAuth field clears it, and a saved key or secret
has a **Remove** button. A cleared value is kept in `config.json` under
`clearedSettings`, out of sight: no page shows it and no run uses it.

A field that an environment variable or a `serve` flag sets is shown locked,
with the name that sets it, because saving it here would change nothing.

Every field shows its CLI flag under it, so what the dashboard does can be
scripted with `set` and `set --repo`. **Repository settings** carries the
repository's own provider and models (**AI for this repository**) and the
review settings `set --repo` writes (**Review tools and limits**). The other
way round, `set --repo` writes the switches the dashboard keeps:
`--auto-review`, `--review-scope`, `--skip-drafts`, `--skip-bots`,
`--codegraph`, `--watch-open-issues`, `--watch-push-mode`, `--review-policy`
and `--remake-cron`, also while `serve` is running.

A **Search settings** box above the Settings menu finds a setting by its name or
description as you type. Arrow keys move, `Enter` opens, and the page scrolls to
the field, focuses it and marks it for a moment.

Settings pages and **Repository settings** show their save state at the top:
**Unsaved changes** once a field changed, **Saving** while a save runs, **All
changes saved** when nothing is left, and **Not saved** when a save failed.

## Audit log

**Settings**, **Audit log** lists who did what and when:

- settings and repository settings changes, with each changed setting and its old
  and new value
- remote tokens created, turned on or off, and deleted
- repositories added and removed
- sign-ins, with the password or with GitHub
- reviews started by hand and failures retried
- failures dismissed
- updates started

A secret never shows a value, old or new, only that it changed. A GitHub sign-in
names the GitHub login, so the log names the person. The list filters by kind and
person and is paged.

## Updates

**Check for new versions** at the bottom of the sidebar checks by hand, on any
server. It first says that it asks github.com, and only after **Check now** does
it read the latest release and `CHANGELOG.md`. The dialog then lists each newer
version with one short line per change, and a link to the full changelog.
Nothing about the server is sent. **Star Co-Maintainer** below it opens
the repository on GitHub.

The automatic newer version check runs only when the host sets `CM_UPDATE_URL`.
Without it the server never calls out on its own, and **Settings**, **Server**, **Updates** shows the
lines that update a self-hosted Docker server:

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/groophylifefor/co-maintainer:latest
docker stop co-maintainer
docker rm co-maintainer
docker run -d --name co-maintainer -p 5000:5000 \
  -v co-maintainer-data:/data \
  ghcr.io/groophylifefor/co-maintainer:latest
```

Start the container with the options you started it with, on the same volume.

With `CM_UPDATE_URL` set, the server reads the latest stable release from GitHub
at most once a day and keeps the answer beside `app.db`. When a newer one is out,
the sidebar and the **Updates** card say "co-maintainer 0.7.15 is out. This
instance runs 0.7.14." with a link to its release notes. **Update to 0.7.15**
POSTs `{"version":"0.7.15","current":"0.7.14"}` to `CM_UPDATE_URL`, the host
restarts the instance on that image, and the card shows the update until the new
version answers, then reloads. The button only offers the latest release newer
than the running one, never an older version. Each update started is written to
the [Audit log](#audit-log). See [Cloud: Versions and updates](cloud.md#versions-and-updates).

## Who gets a review

Each repository has a **Who gets a review** card under its **Settings**. It is
where the [review policy](review-policy.md) lives. The summary under **In short**
says in plain sentences what the current choice does, and it updates as you edit
the rules. **Save** stays off while the policy is not valid and the message says
what to fix. A repository on **Simple switches** shows the three switches it had
before. One on a policy shows **How reviews run**, which holds only the review
scope and codegraph.

On **Activity**, **Pull requests we skipped** names the rule that decided, and a
pull request that is waiting for a request has a **Review now** button.

## Custom review instructions

Each repository also has a **Custom review instructions** card under its
**Settings**. The text is added to the reviewer's built-in instructions for
every review of that repository, as a `CUSTOM REVIEW INSTRUCTIONS` section.
Leave it blank for none. **Maximum characters** caps the text, defaults to 8000,
and `0` or `-1` means no limit. The command line form and the per-run flags are
on [Review](review.md#repository-review-instructions).

## Extension results

Each round on the pull request page lists the [extensions](extensions.md) that
ran in it. For each one the page shows the outcome, the reason when it failed or
skipped, media links, metrics, its findings with their state (`new`, `still open`
or `closed`), its Markdown, and the captured output of a failure. The round's
cost column notes `incl. $X extensions` when an extension reported a cost.

## Clearing knowledge

**Knowledge** carries a **Clear knowledge** card: it deletes that repository's
guides and saved settings, and a checkbox also drops the cached evidence
(pull request listings, cost estimates, clones and worktrees). The spend
history on Usage stays. The next **Sync** builds
the knowledge from scratch. See [Caching: Clearing](caching.md#clearing).

**Settings**, **Danger zone** has **Clear all knowledge**, which does the same for every
repository on the server. Repository records, review history and tokens stay.
Both actions ask about work in flight first: queued jobs are canceled, a
running review can be stopped, and a running sync is waited out because it
cannot be interrupted. Nothing is deleted until that question is answered.

## UI behavior

- Failed API calls show a toast and **Retry**.
- Toggles roll back if save fails.
- [`serve --inject-500`](serve.md#parameters) (or `CM_INJECT_500=1`) forces mutating
  `/api/*` calls except login to fail, for testing error UI.

## Linux

Linux (WSL included) is the recommended platform for [`serve`](serve.md) and the
dashboard:

- SQLite FFI, advisory locks, and POSIX signals behave more predictably.
- Windows is supported but treated as unstable.
- `serve` logs a one-line warning when not on Linux.

## Updating

See [Updates](#updates) for the notice and the button. Forward-only `app.db` migrations. Do not downgrade the CLI after a newer version
has run.

1. Stop `serve`.
2. `npm install -g co-maintainer@latest`
3. Start `serve` again with the same data directory.

Restart after upgrading. Details also on [`serve`: Updating](serve.md#updating).

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/github-app.md

# GitHub App

Automatic pull request reviews, webhooks, and the dashboard repositories all run
through one GitHub App. The dashboard can create it for you, so the private key,
webhook secret, and OAuth credentials are written straight into `config.json`
instead of being copied between two screens.

[`serve`](serve.md) runs the App. The App is **not** the same as CLI `gh` auth,
which is only for reading a repository locally. See
[Authentication](authentication.md) for the full picture.

## Create it from the dashboard

1. Start [`serve`](serve.md) and open the dashboard.
2. Set a public webhook address under **Settings**, **GitHub**.
3. In the GitHub App card, keep or edit the suggested name and press
   **Create GitHub App**.
4. GitHub shows the permissions and events listed below and asks you to confirm.
5. GitHub redirects back, and `serve` writes the App ID, private key, webhook
   secret, and OAuth client ID and secret into `config.json`.

The suggested name is `co-maintainer-<host>`, shortened to fit GitHub's 34
character cap. App names are globally unique, so GitHub rejects a duplicate and
the field stays editable. The button is refused, with the reason, until the
webhook address looks reachable from GitHub. See
[Dashboard: Webhook reachability](dashboard.md#webhook-reachability).

The creation is secured with a single-use server-side state that expires after
ten minutes, so the callback cannot be replayed.

## Install it on repositories

Creating the App does not install it. In GitHub, install the App on the
organization or account that owns your repositories, and choose which
repositories it can reach. The dashboard's **Add repository** list shows only
repositories the App can already see.

## Permissions

The manifest requests exactly the permissions the code uses, not a superset.

<!-- permissions:app:start -->
| Permission | Access | Why |
| ---------- | ------ | --- |
| Contents | Read | Read files and PR_REVIEW_GUIDE.md, read the file tree, read commit history, compare two commits, read releases in the probe |
| Issues | Read and write | Read the conversation on a pull request, post a conversation comment, open an issue for a P0 or P1 commit watch finding, see whether a commit watch issue was closed, close a commit watch issue once its finding is fixed, create the co-maintainer and cm-P0 / cm-P1 labels, acknowledge a review request on the pull request, edit the failure note left on a pull request, acknowledge a review request in a comment |
| Pull requests | Read and write | List pull requests, read a pull request, read the files a pull request changes, read earlier reviews, read review comment threads, post a review, reply in a review comment thread |
| Checks | Read and write | Create the review check run, update the review check run |
| Metadata | Read | Read the repository and its default branch, check a commenter has write access before acting on a comment |
<!-- permissions:app:end -->

Metadata is required by every GitHub App. The review check run is created
through the App, never with a personal access token.

No `administration`, no `actions`, and no `packages` access is requested.

## Events

| Event | Why it is subscribed |
| ----- | -------------------- |
| `pull_request` | Open, synchronize, and close decide whether a review runs |
| `pull_request_review` | Tracks review state for the auto-review rules |
| `pull_request_review_comment` | Delivers a reply in an existing review comment thread |
| `issue_comment` | Delivers a reply in a pull request conversation, and a comment on a [commit watch](commit-watch-review.md) issue |

`push` is **not** subscribed by default. Tick it under **Subscribe to events**
in the App's settings to turn on [commit watch](commit-watch-review.md) through
the App. That applies to every repository the App is installed on, and the App
reviews pushes to each repository's default branch only.

`installation` and `installation_repositories` are handled too, but they are
**not** in the subscription list: GitHub delivers both to every App without a
subscription, which is why the webhook handler accepts them.

A repository removed from the App's installation on GitHub stops being
reviewed. When it is added back, or the App is uninstalled and installed again,
it stays off: removing a repository usually means stopping its reviews and
their cost, so it never comes back on without a word. The dashboard's
**Repositories** page shows "This repository is back in the installation" with
a **Resume reviews** button. Resume turns reviews on again with the knowledge it
had, so no init runs, and opens its Knowledge page with what changed since and
the usual Sync. A repository you removed from the dashboard yourself gets no
such notice. The return and the resume are both in the audit log.

## Diagrams in App reviews

An App review has no command line, so it reads the diagram settings saved for the
repository: `co-maintainer set --repo=owner/repo --diagram-runtime=...`. With
`plantuml-server` the diagram source of a private repository is in a URL that
readers' browsers send to that server, see
[Diagrams](review.md#with-plantuml-server-the-diagram-source-leaves-your-machine).
See [Configuration](configuration.md#diagram-settings) for the settings and for
what happens to a bad stored value.

## Extensions in App reviews

An App review runs the [extensions](extensions.md) registered on this `serve`
host, and the review body shows their results.

- A finding on a diff line is posted inline, headed
  `[P1 · blocking] · extension: NAME`. A finding off the diff goes in the summary
  list. At most 50 extension comments go inline and 50 findings are listed, then
  `- and N more, see the dashboard`. A title is cut at 200 characters in the list
  and a body at 4,000 characters inline.
- An `#### Extensions` section comes before Metadata, with each extension's
  Markdown in a `<details>` block. Metadata gains `- Extensions: [..]`,
  `- Failed Extensions: [..]`, `- Skipped Extensions: [..]` and
  `- Requested changes: [..]`.
- A failed extension is named as "NAME extension failed, you can see details in
  dashboard". It never blocks the review.
- One extension's `request_changes` makes the review type Request changes.
- The review body stays under 250,000 characters. Over that, the longest
  extension Markdown is replaced with "Not added to this comment because of the
  length limit, see the dashboard.", then the next longest, until it fits. The AI
  review is never cut.
- `serve` removes the extension run folders of jobs that are not running when it
  starts, and only folders co-maintainer made.

`CM_EXTENSIONS_DISABLED=1` on the host turns all of this off.

## Companions in App reviews

A review can read the pull requests of other repositories that belong to the
same change, such as the docs or an editor extension, as context. List them
with `co-maintainer set --repo=owner/app --companions=owner/docs,owner/vscode-ext`,
and link a pull request with a `Companion: owner/docs#112` line in its body. A
listed repository without a line is matched by the same head branch name.

The App must be installed on each companion repository. A companion no
installation can read gives the warning `companion_unreachable` in the job log,
and the review goes on without it. See
[Companion pull requests](companions.md#companion-pull-requests).

## Manual setup

If you would rather create the App by hand, use the same values:

```sh
co-maintainer set --github-app-id=... --github-app-private-key-path=./app.pem
co-maintainer set --github-webhook-secret=...
co-maintainer set --github-oauth-client-id=... --github-oauth-client-secret=...
co-maintainer set --github-oauth-allowed-user=your-github-login
```

Set the webhook URL to `https://<your-host>/github/webhook` and subscribe to the
four events above. [Configuration](configuration.md#co-maintainer-set) lists every flag and the
three ways to supply the private key. OAuth is optional and only gates the
dashboard sign-in. See [`serve`: Sign in](serve.md#sign-in-to-the-dashboard).

## Rotating and moving the key

`--github-app-private-key-file` copies the key into `config.json`, so it keeps
working if the file moves. `--github-app-private-key-path` stores only the path,
so the secret never enters `config.json` and `serve` reads it at startup. If that
file is missing, `serve` warns and continues. See
[Configuration: App private key](configuration.md#app-private-key-inline-file-contents-or-path).

If a new key is generated in GitHub, save it and run the `set` command again, or
paste it into Settings. Credentials are read on every request, so the change
applies without a restart.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
| ------- | --- |
| **Create GitHub App** is refused | Set a public webhook address first |
| App created but no review arrives | Install the App on the repository, turn on auto-review in repo **Settings**, and confirm the webhook delivered |
| Settings save returns `422` | The key or token is missing a scope GitHub requires |
| Webhook works but no review is posted | Check the Activity job log, then the AI key and models under **Settings** |
| A failed review blocks the merge | The owner can comment `/co-maintainer skip-this-commit` on the pull request, see [Skipping a failed review](review-policy.md#skipping-a-failed-review) |
| The server is down and its review blocks the merge | Dismiss the App's review on GitHub, see [When the server is down](review-policy.md#when-the-server-is-down) |
| A private repository is reviewed from the diff alone | The review clones with the App's installation token. Check that the App is installed on the repository with **Contents: Read** |

Webhook reachability problems are shown on each repository's **Overview** tab.
See [Dashboard: Webhook reachability](dashboard.md#webhook-reachability).

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/cloud.md

# Cloud

The hosted service at `cloud.co-maintainer.com` runs [`serve`](serve.md) for
you, so your team gets shared repository context without operating a server.
This page explains how it relates to the CLI and the self-hosted setup.

Self-hosting stays supported. Cloud is the same binary with the same database
and the same remote review API, only managed for you.

## What cloud gives you

| Piece | Detail |
| ----- | ------ |
| Managed `serve` | The [dashboard](dashboard.md), the job worker, and the webhook receiver |
| Per-team instances | Each team gets its own instance and host name |
| Repository context | [`init`](init.md) and [`sync`](sync.md) run on the instance, not on every laptop |
| Remote review | Developers keep using `review --remote` against the instance |
| GitHub App | Created from the dashboard, the same flow as self-hosted |

## Connecting the CLI

The connection is identical to a self-hosted server: a host and a `cmr_` token.

1. Sign in to your instance and open **Settings**, **Remote review**.
2. Create a token and copy it once.
3. On the laptop:

```sh
co-maintainer set --remote-host=https://<your-instance> --remote-token=cmr_...
cd your/clone
co-maintainer review --remote
```

The CLI needs no local `init` for that repository, because the guides live on
the instance. See [Remote review](remote-review.md) for the full flag list and
the codegraph behavior, and [Authentication](authentication.md) for how the
token fits with the other credentials.

You can read the exact guides your review will use before running it:

```sh
co-maintainer view owner/repo --remote
```

## Putting a repository on the instance

Open the dashboard, choose **Add repository**, and confirm the plan. This is the
same flow as self-hosted, including the read-only probe and the cost estimate.
The dashboard needs the GitHub App installed on the repository, which the
**Create GitHub App** button sets up for you.

## Mixing cloud with local CLI

A team can keep using the CLI for local and PR review while cloud holds the
shared context. The two do not conflict:

| If you want | Run it |
| ----------- | ------ |
| Feedback on your working tree, before a push | `review` with local guides |
| Feedback using the team's shared context | `review --remote` against the instance |
| A PR reviewed automatically | The GitHub App on the instance |
| A repository onboarded once for everyone | Dashboard **Add repository** |

## Extensions are off

[Extensions](extensions.md) are always off in the cloud. The hosted service sets
`CM_EXTENSIONS_DISABLED=1` from outside the container, so nothing in your data
can turn them on.

## MCP servers are off

[MCP servers](review.md#mcp-servers) are always off in the cloud. The hosted
service sets `CM_MCP_DISABLED=1` from outside the container, so
`set --mcp-config` is refused and no review starts an MCP server.

## Versions and updates

An instance runs the image the host deployed. Each stable release publishes
`ghcr.io/groophylifefor/co-maintainer:<version>` and `:latest`.

The host sets `CM_UPDATE_URL` on the instance. With it, the dashboard reads the
latest stable release from GitHub at most once a day and keeps the answer. When
a newer one is out, admins see "co-maintainer 0.7.15 is out. This instance runs
0.7.14." in the sidebar and under **Settings**, **Server**, **Updates**, with a
link to the release notes.

**Update to 0.7.15** sends a `POST` to `CM_UPDATE_URL` with a JSON body:

```json
{"version":"0.7.15","current":"0.7.14"}
```

Any `2xx` answer means the host took the request. The host restarts the instance
on that image, and the card shows the update until the new version answers. Any
other answer, or no answer, shows that the update did not start. The button only
offers the latest stable release newer than the running one, never an older
version, and every update started is written to the [Audit log](dashboard.md#audit-log).

Without `CM_UPDATE_URL` the instance never asks for the latest release, and
Settings shows the `docker pull` and restart lines a self-hosted server uses. See
[Dashboard: Updates](dashboard.md#updates).

## Support and status

The instance list, uptime, and any incident notes are published by the
co-maintainer maintainers. For a self-hosted deployment, the same pages under
[Serve](serve.md) and the [Dashboard](dashboard.md) apply.

If a remote review fails, [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) lists the token
and connectivity messages, and [Data and privacy](../privacy.html) says what the
instance stores.

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/commands.md

# Commands

Reference for every visible command. This page is generated from the command
registry in the source, so it always matches `co-maintainer help` and
`co-maintainer help <command>`.

## `co-maintainer probe`

Inspect a repository and recommend the init flags for it.

```
co-maintainer probe owner/repo [options]
```

### GitHub access

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--auth=gh\|pat` | gh | Use the gh CLI or a personal access token. |
| `--github-pat=TOKEN` |  | The token when --auth=pat. |

### Limits

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--max-pull-request-change-lines=N` |  | Cap the diff size sampled. |
| `--max-pr-months=N` |  | Cap how far back pull requests are read. |
| `--max-commits=N` |  | Cap how many commits are read. |

### After the plan

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--run` |  | Run the recommended init in this same process. |

### Output and diagnostics

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | Print machine-readable JSON instead of prose. |
| `--debug` |  | Print the underlying gh and HTTP calls. |
| `--log-time` |  | Print how long each phase took. |
| `--env=PATH` |  | Read environment variables from a .env file first. A variable already set wins. |

## `co-maintainer init`

Build the review guides for a repository for the first time.

```
co-maintainer init owner/repo [options]
```

### Sources

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--include-codebase` |  | Read the source tree. |
| `--include-pull-requests` |  | Read pull request history. |
| `--include-pull-request-changes` |  | Read the diffs of those pull requests. |
| `--include-commit-history` |  | Read commit history. |
| `--include-how-repo-works` |  | Read the docs and layout. |
| `--agent-instructions=REGEX` | (^\|/)AGENTS\.md$ | Paths on the default branch to read as agent instruction files for INSTRUCTIONS.md. Needs --include-codebase. A blank value turns it off. Saved for later syncs. |

### Limits

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--max-commits=N` | all | Cap how many commits are read. |
| `--agent-instructions-max-chars=N` | 6000 | Cap on INSTRUCTIONS.md in characters. 0 or below means no limit. Saved for later syncs. |
| `--max-pr-months=N` | all | Cap how far back pull requests are read. |
| `--max-pull-request-change-lines=N` | all | Cap the diff size read. |
| `--max-comment=N` |  | Cap the comments read per pull request. |

### Pull request filter

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--pr-state=open,closed,merged` |  | Which pull request states to read. |
| `--only-request-changed-pr` |  | Read only the pull requests with at least one CHANGES_REQUESTED review. Saved for the repository. |
| `--no-only-request-changed-pr` |  | Read every pull request again, turning a saved --only-request-changed-pr off. |

### AI

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ai=openrouter\|openai\|anthropic\|opencode-zen\|opencode-go` |  | Which provider writes the guides. Required: init and sync cannot run without one. |
| `--token=KEY` |  | The provider API key. |
| `--ai-key=KEY` |  | The same key as --token, named for what it is. |
| `--low-model=ID` |  | Model for extraction work. |
| `--high-model=ID` |  | Model for the review itself. |

### Experimental

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--experimental-siwc` |  | Run on your ChatGPT plan through Sign in with ChatGPT instead of an API key. Cannot be combined with --ai. Set up with co-maintainer oauth. |

### GitHub access

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--auth=gh\|pat` | gh | Use the gh CLI or a personal access token. |
| `--github-pat=TOKEN` |  | The token when --auth=pat. |

### Output and diagnostics

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | Print machine-readable JSON instead of prose. |
| `--debug` |  | Print the underlying gh and HTTP calls. |
| `--log-time` |  | Print how long each phase took. |
| `--env=PATH` |  | Read environment variables from a .env file first. A variable already set wins. |

### Performance

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--gh-concurrent=N` | 1 | Concurrent GitHub calls for this run only. It does not change the saved default. |
| `--ai-concurrent=N` | 3 | Concurrent AI calls for this run only. It does not change the saved default. |

## `co-maintainer sync`

Rebuild the review guides for a repository that already has them.

```
co-maintainer sync owner/repo [options]
```

### Sources

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--include-codebase` |  | Read the source tree. |
| `--include-pull-requests` |  | Read pull request history. |
| `--include-pull-request-changes` |  | Read the diffs of those pull requests. |
| `--include-commit-history` |  | Read commit history. |
| `--include-how-repo-works` |  | Read the docs and layout. |
| `--agent-instructions=REGEX` |  | Paths on the default branch to read as agent instruction files for INSTRUCTIONS.md. Needs --include-codebase. A blank value turns it off. Left out, the last run's value is kept. |

### Limits

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|

| `--agent-instructions-max-chars=N` |  | Cap on INSTRUCTIONS.md in characters. 0 or below means no limit. Left out, the last run's value is kept. |
| `--max-pr-months=N` |  | Cap how far back pull requests are read. |
| `--max-pull-request-change-lines=N` |  | Cap the diff size read. |
| `--max-comment=N` |  | Cap the comments read per pull request. |

### Pull request filter

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--pr-state=open,closed,merged` |  | Which pull request states to read. |
| `--only-request-changed-pr` |  | Read only the pull requests with at least one CHANGES_REQUESTED review. Saved for the repository. |
| `--no-only-request-changed-pr` |  | Read every pull request again, turning a saved --only-request-changed-pr off. |

### AI

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ai=openrouter\|openai\|anthropic\|opencode-zen\|opencode-go` |  | Which provider writes the guides. Required: init and sync cannot run without one. |
| `--token=KEY` |  | The provider API key. |
| `--ai-key=KEY` |  | The same key as --token, named for what it is. |
| `--low-model=ID` |  | Model for extraction work. |
| `--high-model=ID` |  | Model for the review itself. |

### Experimental

| Flag | Default | Description |

### GitHub access

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--auth=gh\|pat` | gh | Use the gh CLI or a personal access token. |
| `--github-pat=TOKEN` |  | The token when --auth=pat. |

### Output and diagnostics

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | Print machine-readable JSON instead of prose. |
| `--debug` |  | Print the underlying gh and HTTP calls. |
| `--log-time` |  | Print how long each phase took. |

### Performance

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--gh-concurrent=N` | 1 | Concurrent GitHub calls for this run only. It does not change the saved default. |
| `--ai-concurrent=N` | 3 | Concurrent AI calls for this run only. It does not change the saved default. |

### Review guide

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--full-guide` |  | Rewrite the review guide in full now, instead of editing it, and start the count of --guide-full-every again. |

## `co-maintainer review`

Review a pull request, or the local changes in this workspace.

```
co-maintainer review owner/repo PR_NUMBER [options]
co-maintainer review [options]
```

### Target

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--repo=owner/repo` |  | The repository the local changes belong to. |
| `--branch=NAME` |  | The branch the local changes are on. |
| `--to-branch=NAME` |  | Compare the local changes against this branch. |
| `--fresh` |  | Ignore the previous review and start over. |

### Local only

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--remote` |  | Send the diff to the configured remote server instead of reviewing locally. |
| `--remote-host=URL` |  | Override the configured remote host for this run (needs --remote). |
| `--remote-token=TOKEN` |  | Override the configured remote token for this run (needs --remote). |
| `--remote-byok` |  | Send your own AI key with a remote review (needs --remote). |
| `--no-remote-byok` |  | Do not send your own AI key, even if remote-byok-default is on. |
| `--sync-before-review` |  | Rebuild the guides before reviewing. |

### Codegraph

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--disable-codegraph` |  | Skip the codegraph index. |
| `--allow-tool-install` |  | Install codegraph if it is missing. |

### Custom instructions

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--system-prompt-file=PATH` |  | Append this file's contents to the review instructions for this run only. |
| `--system-prompt-override-file=PATH` |  | Replace the repository's review instructions with this file for this run only. The built-in instructions are kept. |
| `--range=BEFORE..AFTER` |  | With --remote: review a push (commit watch). The server keeps the review going if this run stops waiting. |
| `--timeout-minutes=N` |  | With --range: stop waiting after N minutes and leave the result to the dashboard, default 10. With --remote on a pull request: fail with exit code 3 after N minutes, no limit by default. |

### Intent

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--intent-file=PATH` |  | Tell the review what the change is for, from a file or from standard input with -. It is context only, never a rule. Up to the repository's custom prompt cap. Not with --range. |

### Companions

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--with=PATH[@BRANCH]` |  | Read the changes of another checkout as context, such as the docs or a client of this code. Without @BRANCH its current branch and working tree, with @BRANCH that branch against its default branch, without a checkout. Repeat it for each companion, up to 5. Not with --range. |

### Diagrams

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--diagram-runtime=mermaid\|plantuml\|plantuml-server` | mermaid | The diagram language the review uses. plantuml keeps the PlantUML source. plantuml-server turns it into an image link on a PlantUML server. Not with --remote. |
| `--plantuml-server=URL` | https://www.plantuml.com | The PlantUML server for plantuml-server. An http or https URL. The diagram source travels in the image link. |
| `--plantuml-output-format=svg\|png` | svg | The image format for plantuml-server. |

### Depth

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--improve-matrix=N` | 1 | How many passes the review model makes over its own findings. Capped at 4, and each pass costs more. |
| `--review-upstream` |  | On a pull request, review the code merged in from the base branch too, not only what the author wrote. |

### AI

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ai=openrouter\|openai\|anthropic\|opencode-zen\|opencode-go` |  | Which provider writes the review. With no provider saved, OpenRouter. A review cannot run without one. |
| `--token=KEY` |  | The provider API key. |
| `--ai-key=KEY` |  | The same key as --token, named for what it is. |
| `--low-model=ID` |  | Model for extraction work. |
| `--high-model=ID` |  | Model for the review itself. |

### Experimental

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--experimental-siwc` |  | Run on your ChatGPT plan through Sign in with ChatGPT instead of an API key. Cannot be combined with --ai. Set up with co-maintainer oauth. |

### GitHub access

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--auth=gh\|pat` | gh | Use the gh CLI or a personal access token. |
| `--github-pat=TOKEN` |  | The token when --auth=pat. |

### Output and diagnostics

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | Print machine-readable JSON instead of prose. |
| `--debug` |  | Print the underlying gh and HTTP calls. |
| `--log-time` |  | Print how long each phase took. |
| `--env=PATH` |  | Read environment variables from a .env file first. A variable already set wins. |
| `--output=github` |  | Print GitHub workflow annotations and write the job summary instead of prose. Cannot be used with --json. |
| `--include-extension-markdowns` |  | With --json, keep each extension's markdown. It is empty otherwise. |


### Guides

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--list` |  | List the guide files with their size and build date. |
| `--sources` |  | List every guide and instruction rule by id, with the pull requests or instruction file lines it came from. |
| `--json` |  | With --sources, print RULES.json as it is. |
| `--path` |  | Print the directory the guides live in. |
| `--remote` |  | Read the guides from the configured remote review server instead. |
